bottom_line: The Fed (the people who set interest rates) held steady in October, but its meeting notes show almost all officials expect to raise rates again, possibly in December, because prices are still rising too fast. Higher rates make loans, credit cards and mortgages cost more, and the S&P 500 broke a key support level on the news.

stories.title: Fed says more rate hikes coming
stories.real: In October the Fed held its main rate between 3.75% and 4%, but the notes from that meeting show almost all officials expect more hikes, and some wanted a bigger one. Fed governor Waller said they may need to 'shock people' with a half-point hike, and officials are also worried about how AI could affect inflation.
stories.you: Borrowing is likely to stay expensive or get more expensive, so car loans, credit cards and mortgages won't get cheaper soon.

stories.title: Anthropic's record stock market debut
stories.real: Anthropic, the five-year-old AI company that makes Claude, raised a record $81.3 billion by selling shares at $83 each, beating SpaceX's offering. It starts trading on the Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT and is valued at up to $1.5tn, even with growing fears of an AI bubble.
stories.you: Lots of regular investors are excited about it, but a hyped first day says nothing about whether a stock is a good long-term deal, and new stocks can swing hard.

stories.title: Nvidia beats, stock slips anyway
stories.real: Nvidia posted strong results, but the stock slipped because Jensen Huang has left as CEO and its China business carries risk. Interim CEO Colette Kress offered staff pay raises and told them 'let's move forward,' while stocks fell and the dollar hit a 19-month high.
stories.you: If you own tech-heavy funds, good earnings alone aren't holding prices up right now, because worries about leadership, China and AI debt are weighing on them.

stories.title: Australia's jobs market cracks
stories.real: Australia's economy lost 43,500 jobs and unemployment jumped to 4.9%, the highest since 2021, after its central bank raised rates. That's what rate hikes can do: they cool prices by slowing the economy, and that costs jobs.
stories.you: It's a real example of the tradeoff the US Fed is weighing: higher rates can tame prices, but they can also put people out of work.

stories.title: UK prices rising again
stories.real: UK inflation hit a 1-year high of 3.6%, driven by record diesel prices and high gas prices. The typical household energy bill is forecast to rise by £443 a year from January, a 26% jump.
stories.you: Energy costs are pushing up prices in other countries too, which is part of why central banks are leaning toward higher rates.
